assertion_audit: tests/test_estimator_scoreboard.py:394-400: restoring scalar fallback makes both nan checks and the false q95 verdict fail; changing other metric calculations breaks the remaining-band all assertion.

tests/test_estimator_scoreboard.py:415-428: dropping the IMAS map breaks is-not-None; returning nan breaks finite; ignoring or reversing the gradient breaks stronger > value > 0. These are directional checks, not an absolute numerical oracle.

tests/test_estimator_scoreboard.py:434-436: is-None and finite stored q establish the no-map positive fixture; returning that scalar from the calculator breaks the nan assertion, demonstrated in negative-control.log.

tests/test_estimator_scoreboard.py:454-481: CLI status fails on scoring failure; persisted nan value/metric and false verdict fail if scalar fallback or omitted q95_values is restored; stored-q comparison is now independently calculated from fixture profile nodes and breaks reader interpolation/value corruption; removing absence rendering breaks the HTML text checks.

tests/test_estimator_scoreboard.py:502-506: finite checks reject invalid geometry; resetting flux_map_scale to 1 breaks the registered-bound comparison; ignoring q95_values breaks the false verdict because the stored profiles are equal. The measured q values do not constitute the expected threshold, so this is not a same-input tautology.

tests/test_estimator_scoreboard.py:532-548: map presence, descending levels and descending stored nodes validate the fixture orientation; finite/positive rejects invalid output; sorting physical nodes before normalisation breaks equality against the independently negated map, as negative-control-round2.log shows; discarding the inward tail breaks gradient growth.

tests/test_estimator_scoreboard.py:563-572: dropping maps breaks presence; applying a zero perturbation incorrectly to scalar levels breaks approximate equality; restoring division by abs(span) breaks map and gradient-node allclose, as negative-control-round2.log shows; changing q_scale default breaks stored-q identity.

No remaining added assertion compares a scorer readback with the same reader as its expected scalar: the earlier stored-q assertion now constructs its expectation directly from the fixture q-profile values.
